Title: Verify successful login with valid credentials redirects to Dashboard and creates a session
Precondition: The OrangeHRM QA login page is reachable at https://opensource-demo.orangehrmlive.com/web/index.php/auth/login. A registered user account exists with username 'Admin' and password 'admin123'. No active session exists in the browser.
Steps: 1. Navigate to https://opensource-demo.orangehrmlive.com/web/index.php/auth/login → Expected: Login page loads over HTTPS displaying the OrangeHRM logo, Username field, Password field, Login button, and 'Forgot your password?' link | 2. Enter 'Admin' into the field labelled 'Username' → Expected: The Username field shows 'Admin' and no validation message is displayed | 3. Enter 'admin123' into the field labelled 'Password' → Expected: The Password field shows masked characters and no validation message is displayed | 4. Click the 'Login' button → Expected: The user is authenticated and redirected to the Dashboard at /web/index.php/dashboard/index within 3 seconds, with the top navigation and Dashboard widgets visible
Expected Result: The registered user is authenticated, redirected to the Dashboard, and a valid authenticated session is established.

Title: Verify login fails with 'Invalid credentials' when password is wrong
Precondition: The OrangeHRM QA login page is reachable. A registered user account exists with username 'Admin' and password 'admin123'. No active session exists.
Steps: 1. Navigate to https://opensource-demo.orangehrmlive.com/web/index.php/auth/login → Expected: Login page is displayed with Username and Password fields and the Login button | 2. Enter 'Admin' into the Username field → Expected: The Username field shows 'Admin' | 3. Enter 'wrongPass999' into the Password field → Expected: The Password field shows masked characters | 4. Click the 'Login' button → Expected: An 'Invalid credentials' error banner is displayed, the URL remains on /auth/login, and no session is created
Expected Result: Authentication is rejected, the 'Invalid credentials' error is shown, and the user stays on the login page.

Enter 'admin123' into the Password field → Expected: The Password field shows masked characters | 4. Click the 'Login' button → Expected: An 'Invalid credentials' error is displayed and the user remains on the login page with no session created

Click the 'Login' button → Expected: A 'Required' validation message is displayed directly beneath the Username field, no request to authenticate is made, and the user stays on the login page
Expected Result: A field-level 'Required' message is shown for Username and authentication does not proceed.

Title: Verify Password field masks characters as they are typed
Precondition: The OrangeHRM QA login page is reachable and no active session exists.
Steps: 1. Navigate to the login page → Expected: Login form is displayed | 2. Type 'Secr3t!Pass' into the Password field → Expected: Each typed character is rendered as a masked dot/bullet rather than the literal character | 3. Inspect the Password input element's type attribute via browser DevTools → Expected: The input element has type='password', confirming the value is not exposed as plain text in the DOM rendering
Expected Result: The password value is displayed only as masked characters and never as readable plain text.

Title: Verify Logout returns the user to the Login page and terminates the session
Precondition: A registered user is logged in as 'Admin' and is currently on the Dashboard with an active session.
Steps: 1. From the Dashboard, click the user dropdown menu in the top-right header → Expected: A dropdown menu opens showing 'About', 'Support', 'Change Password', and 'Logout' options | 2. Click the 'Logout' option → Expected: The session is ended and the browser is redirected to the login page at /web/index.php/auth/login
Expected Result: The user session is terminated and the login page is displayed.

Title: Verify browser Back button after Logout does not restore the cached Dashboard
Precondition: A registered user has just logged out and is on the login page. The Dashboard was previously visited in this browser tab's history.
Steps: 1. Confirm the current page is the login page immediately after logout → Expected: The login form is displayed | 2. Click the browser Back button → Expected: The authenticated Dashboard is NOT restored from cache; the user is kept on or redirected back to the login page | 3. Attempt to interact with any control that would require an active session → Expected: No protected Dashboard content is accessible; the user must re-authenticate
Expected Result: The Back button does not expose the cached Dashboard; the invalidated session forces re-authentication.

Title: Verify direct navigation to a protected Dashboard URL without a session redirects to Login
Precondition: No user is logged in and no active session cookie exists in the browser.
Steps: 1. Ensure no session exists by clearing cookies or opening a fresh private window → Expected: No authenticated session is present | 2. Navigate directly to https://opensource-demo.orangehrmlive.com/web/index.php/dashboard/index → Expected: The application redirects to the login page at /web/index.php/auth/login and does not render any Dashboard content
Expected Result: Access to the protected Dashboard without a session is denied and the user is redirected to Login.

Title: Verify leading and trailing spaces in Username are trimmed before authentication
Precondition: The OrangeHRM QA login page is reachable. A registered account exists with username 'Admin' and password 'admin123'. No active session exists.
Steps: 1. Navigate to the login page → Expected: Login form is displayed | 2. Enter '  Admin  ' (with two leading and two trailing spaces) into the Username field → Expected: The Username field accepts the value including surrounding spaces | 3. Enter 'admin123' into the Password field → Expected: The Password field shows masked characters | 4. Click the 'Login' button → Expected: The surrounding spaces are trimmed, the credentials are treated as 'Admin' / 'admin123', and the user is authenticated and redirected to the Dashboard
Expected Result: Username whitespace is trimmed and authentication succeeds.

Title: Verify Password is treated as exact-match with spaces NOT trimmed
Precondition: The OrangeHRM QA login page is reachable. A registered account exists with username 'Admin' and exact password 'admin123' (no surrounding spaces). No active session exists.
Steps: 1. Navigate to the login page → Expected: Login form is displayed | 2. Enter 'Admin' into the Username field → Expected: The Username field shows 'Admin' | 3. Enter ' admin123 ' (with one leading and one trailing space) into the Password field → Expected: The Password field shows masked characters | 4. Click the 'Login' button → Expected: The password is NOT trimmed, so it does not match the stored value; an 'Invalid credentials' error is displayed and the user remains on the login page
Expected Result: The space-padded password is treated as an exact non-matching value and login is rejected.

Title: Verify Username accepts values at the 1-character and 100-character length boundaries
Precondition: The OrangeHRM QA login page is reachable and no active session exists. Test accounts may not exist for these values; the check focuses on field acceptance and validation behavior, not successful authentication.
Steps: 1. Navigate to the login page → Expected: Login form is displayed | 2. Enter the single character 'a' into the Username field, enter 'admin123' into the Password field, and click 'Login' → Expected: The 1-character Username is accepted by the field (no 'Required' or length error); the form submits and returns an 'Invalid credentials' error since the account is unknown | 3. Clear the fields, enter a 100-character string of 'a' into the Username field, enter 'admin123' into the Password field, and click 'Login' → Expected: The 100-character Username is accepted without truncation error; the form submits and returns 'Invalid credentials'
Expected Result: The Username field accepts values at both the 1-character and 100-character boundaries without length-validation errors.

Title: Verify Username input containing an HTML/script payload is sanitized and not executed
Precondition: The OrangeHRM QA login page is reachable and no active session exists.
Steps: 1. Navigate to the login page → Expected: Login form is displayed | 2. Enter the string <script>alert('xss')</script> into the Username field → Expected: The literal characters are shown as text in the field with no dialog triggered on entry | 3. Enter 'admin123' into the Password field and click 'Login' → Expected: No JavaScript alert dialog is executed; the payload is treated as an ordinary (invalid) username and an 'Invalid credentials' error is returned | 4. Confirm the page did not reflect the payload as executable markup by inspecting the rendered response → Expected: The payload is HTML-encoded/sanitized in any reflected output and does not run as script
Expected Result: The injected script is sanitized, never executes, and login is rejected as invalid credentials.

Title: Verify SQL injection payload in login fields does not bypass authentication
Precondition: The OrangeHRM QA login page is reachable and no active session exists.
Steps: 1. Navigate to the login page → Expected: Login form is displayed | 2. Enter admin' OR '1'='1 into the Username field → Expected: The value is accepted as literal text | 3. Enter anything' OR '1'='1 into the Password field and click 'Login' → Expected: Authentication is NOT bypassed; an 'Invalid credentials' error is displayed and the user is not redirected to the Dashboard
Expected Result: The SQL injection attempt fails, returning 'Invalid credentials' with no unauthorized access.

Title: Verify repeated failed login attempts are throttled to prevent brute-force
Precondition: The OrangeHRM QA login page is reachable. A valid account 'Admin' exists but will be targeted with wrong passwords. No active session exists.
Steps: 1. Navigate to the login page → Expected: Login form is displayed | 2. Submit the Login form with username 'Admin' and an incorrect password repeatedly for at least 10 consecutive attempts → Expected: Each attempt returns 'Invalid credentials' | 3. Observe the response behavior across the successive failed attempts → Expected: The application applies a brute-force countermeasure such as a CAPTCHA challenge, an enforced delay, or a temporary lockout, rather than accepting unlimited rapid attempts
Expected Result: Repeated failed attempts trigger a throttling/lockout countermeasure that impedes brute-force guessing.

Title: Verify credentials are transmitted over HTTPS and the password never appears in URL, history, or logs
Precondition: The OrangeHRM QA login page is reachable. A valid account 'Admin' / 'admin123' exists. Browser DevTools Network tab is available for inspection.
Steps: 1. Open browser DevTools, switch to the Network tab, and navigate to the login page → Expected: The page and its resources load over HTTPS (scheme https://) with a valid certificate | 2. Enter 'Admin' and 'admin123', click 'Login', and inspect the authentication request in the Network tab → Expected: The login request is sent over HTTPS using the POST method with credentials in the request body, not in the URL/query string | 3. Inspect the resulting URL and the browser history entry for the request → Expected: Neither the URL nor the browser history contains the password value in plain text | 4. Review any client-accessible console output or response payload → Expected: The password value does not appear in logs, console output, or the response body
Expected Result: The password is transmitted only over HTTPS in the request body and is absent from the URL, browser history, and logs.

Title: Verify Username case-sensitivity behavior matches the configured authentication policy
Precondition: The OrangeHRM QA login page is reachable. A registered account exists with the canonical username 'Admin' and password 'admin123'. The system authentication policy treats the OrangeHRM username as case-sensitive. No active session exists.
Steps: 1. Navigate to the login page → Expected: Login form is displayed | 2. Enter 'admin' (all lowercase) into the Username field and 'admin123' into the Password field → Expected: The fields accept the entered values | 3. Click the 'Login' button → Expected: The outcome matches the configured case-sensitivity policy: for the case-sensitive OrangeHRM policy, 'admin' does not match 'Admin' and an 'Invalid credentials' error is returned rather than a successful login
Expected Result: Username casing is handled per the configured policy, producing a consistent and documented authentication result.
